title: fix(control-ui): avatar picker rejects small images in Safari with a misleading 2 MB error
body:
Closes #154884

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Safari and other WebKit browsers, the agent avatar picker (Settings → Agents → Identity) rejects ordinary images well under 2 MB with "Pick an image file up to 2 MB."

## User Impact

User impact: detailed avatar images now work in WebKit browsers. When an image really can't fit, the error says it's too detailed and points to the CLI, instead of claiming the file is over 2 MB.

Tradeoff: in WebKit, a detailed image with transparency may be stored as a 64 or 48 px PNG instead of 96 px, so it can look slightly soft in the 56 px editor preview on high-DPI screens. Chromium and Firefox are unchanged; they still use 96 px WebP.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker shrinks images to 96 px and keeps the data URL at or under 16,000 characters, because it's mirrored into the prompt-injected `IDENTITY.md`. WebKit ignores `toDataURL("image/webp")` and returns PNG. A detailed 96 px PNG with transparency comes to about 34K characters, so it was rejected. Every rejection reused the 2 MB file-size message.

When WebP isn't available:
- Fully opaque images use JPEG at 96 px.
- Other images are saved as PNG at 96 px, then 64, then 48, and the first one that fits is used.

`fileToAvatarDataUrl` now returns a result that says why it rejected an image: `unusable` (not an image, or over 2 MB) or `too-detailed`. The second maps to a new English string, `agents.identity.imageTooDetailed`. The existing string is unchanged, so its translations stay valid. The 16,000-character limit is also unchanged.

## Evidence

**Maintainer follow-up (September 21):** Current head `0c1f3f6af58ec50e74f63e7164c3ab10d150ce64` includes the avatar wording correction, the already-landed main-side approval fixture repairs, and test-only repairs for migrated-update timeout and retained-grant input failures. Contributor ancestry is preserved.

The migrated-finalization fixture was leaking into host Gateway service discovery. With unavailable native managers, recovery observation outlived the test’s 30-second deadline; local runs misleadingly passed because this host reports an externally supervised Gateway. The fixture now owns that external discovery boundary, using the existing compiled-worker fixture machinery. The actual candidate worker, compatibility check, executor delegation, schema migration, recovery recording, terminal ledger, and existing assertions remain real. Production behavior and timeout values are unchanged.

**New proof:** all 20 migrated-update tests pass under the same unavailable-native-manager setup that reproduced the original timeout; the nine fencing cases complete in 1–4.6 seconds. Independent P0–P2 review of the final five-file fixture repair is scoped-clean. Changed-code checks passed, including all selected typechecks, lint, formatting, dead-export scans and guards. The migrated file measured 58.95 seconds in Vitest and 102.24 seconds through the wrapper including a runtime build. Exact-head CI completed; the updater lanes passed, and the authorized failed-jobs-only rerun below cleared the remaining required gates.

The original seven-file local replay finished with 195 passing and 101 failing tests across three untouched service/ACP/dry-run files; all 20 migrated cases passed. A representative service-ownership failure also reproduces on the untouched main baseline, while ACP startup-migration stderr and dry-run log-state mismatches remain local verification gaps. These are not claimed fixed or hidden by retries. The normal hosted CI and review gates remain mandatory.

ClawSweeper completed review of the exact current `0c1f3f6af58ec50e74f63e7164c3ab10d150ce64` head at 01:23 UTC on September 22 (revision 8) with no actionable findings or security findings. Both required CI gate entries subsequently passed.

The previous head’s avatar unit tests (3/3), i18n and performance checks passed. Its approval-fixture failures are resolved. A separate Collapse-question viewport test intermittently times out after successful click actionability checks, and the runner’s renderer-state read also reaches its deadline. The current run repeats that failure at 430px/light; an earlier run failed at 390px/dark. No browser crash or disconnect was observed.

**Bounded browser investigation:** local replay was blocked by the host’s loopback-HTTP preflight. On configured Blacksmith Testbox, the original shard order on trusted main `267bb9d27fa146e940340a385740b6b54cd86d89`, with CI-pinned Chrome 153.0.8010.12, passed **51 files / 243 tests** (361.85 seconds Vitest). All 15 question tests passed; the four viewport cases took 1.6–2.0 seconds. [Remote run and proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35667945423). The task-owned lease was stopped and verified completed. Source inspection found no established focus/observer feedback loop. This is baseline reproduction evidence, **not a proven fix or exact-current-merge proof**: current CI incorporates later main-side question changes. Product JS starvation versus a Chromium renderer/dispatch hang remains unresolved. No retries, forced clicks, longer timeouts, weakened assertions, or speculative product changes were added. Normal CI and review gates still apply.

The original avatar autoreview’s suggestion to add a WebP size ladder was not included: that path is unchanged from main and explicitly outside this WebKit fallback fix. Both published screenshots were inspected and verified to render in this PR. They cover browser conversion and selection, not unchanged persistence.

**Retained-input fixture follow-up:** [Run 35659800660](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35659800660) cleared the earlier avatar/browser and migrated-finalization blockers, leaving one retained-restart test failure: `readFileSync(0)` encountered `EAGAIN` on a nonblocking delegated-grant input pipe. The current head consumes that same EOF-delimited UTF-8 JSON asynchronously. No production code, authority checks, cleanup assertions, or timeouts changed. All **17 retained-restart tests pass** (31.16 seconds Vitest, 32.73 seconds wrapper); formatting, typed lint, diff-check and independent P0–P2 review pass. The previous auto-merge request was confirmed canceled through the native receipt before replacing its head.

**Final bounded investigations (September 22):** [Current-head CI 35666075111](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35666075111) attempt 1 ended with 109 successful jobs, 14 skipped, two failed test jobs and their failed aggregate gate. Checkout logs bind the failures to synthetic merge `d6c2459de5be1e0205f50440d8ee3b501e5c75c4`, incorporating trusted main `e7f94eb36392ad369b44478f281b9b7af857e530`.

- **Sidebar avatar assertion:** the original 425-file UI group on that trusted base passed **8,129/8,129 tests** (177.15 seconds); the failing priority assertion completed in 53ms. The original preceding security group could not be reproduced cleanly locally (64 failed / 2,737 passed / 11 skipped), so the previously unreached UI group was admitted separately with its original inventory/config/environment. A 484-test full-file diagnostic replay passed and observed registration completing about 14ms after mount, not the CI one-second failure. No stale cache, fetch leak or causal registration fix was established. CI used Node 24.20.0; local Node was 26.8.2; restored caches, worker assignment and contention remain gaps.
- **Current-base browser shard:** the newer 248-test inventory passed **51/51 files and 248/248 tests** with pinned Chrome 153.0.8010.12 on [Blacksmith Testbox run 35673343241](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35673343241), 360.28 seconds Vitest. The entire async-question file passed 19/19; the 430px/light Collapse click resolved in 110ms with input-stage and CPU-profile evidence. Instrumentation can perturb timing; this was the trusted base, not the PR synthetic merge. No failing stack or safe causal fix was established. The owned lease was stopped and verified completed.

These are bounded nonreproductions, not fixes or replacements for the required hosted gate. No speculative patch, assertion weakening or timeout increase was applied. At the requesting maintainer’s direction on September 22, one failed-jobs-only rerun of run 35666075111 was submitted for unchanged head `0c1f3f6af58ec50e74f63e7164c3ab10d150ce64`. Attempt 2 completed successfully at 01:28:42 UTC: 112 successful jobs, 14 skipped, zero failures. Of those successes, 109 carry forward from attempt 1; the retried UI E2E 2/13 and Node compact-large-10 jobs plus their aggregate gate passed. Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` entries were independently verified successful; the separate status completed at 01:29:33 UTC. This does not establish a causal fix for the two unreproduced failures. Native guarded squash-merge recovery completed at 01:35 UTC as [660b69e8e3a52a5d24201bdffe1be8977650fa17](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/660b69e8e3a52a5d24201bdffe1be8977650fa17). The exact reviewed source head was merged, the landed commit is contained in main, and Steve Kinney plus the requested Tak Hoffman co-author trailer were verified from the parsed landed commit message. Required CI/review enforcement was preserved. Post-merge housekeeping: deleting the contributor fork branch was denied, so it remains intact; this does not change the confirmed merge.

**Screenshots:** WebKit 26.6 (Playwright) against `pnpm dev:ui:mock`, picking the same synthetic 512×512 transparent PNG (635 KB):

| Before (`main`) | After (this branch) |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://github.com/stevekinney/openclaw/raw/pr-assets/avatar-picker-154884/before-webkit.png) | ![after](https://github.com/stevekinney/openclaw/raw/pr-assets/avatar-picker-154884/after-webkit.png) |

- **Before:** rejected with "That image can't be used. Pick an image file up to 2 MB."
- **After:** accepted as a 13,418-character PNG data URL, and Save is enabled.
- **WebP probe:** in the same WebKit, `canvas.toDataURL("image/webp")` returned `data:image/png`.
- **Mock gap:** the mock Gateway doesn't advertise `agents.update`, and the page ignores avatar picks without it. The capture script added `agents.update` to the mock's advertised methods in the page before picking. Picking never calls the Gateway.

**Tests:** `pnpm test ui/src/pages/agents/avatar-image.test.ts ui/src/pages/agents/identity-actions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- 15 passed, about 1.5 s of test time and 2.8 s wall time.
- New cases: WebP kept, PNG stepped down to 48 px, JPEG for opaque images, too-detailed after every fallback, non-image rejected as unusable, and a separate error message for each rejection reason.
- The new encoder cases fail against the implementation on `main`.

**Checks:** `pnpm check:changed` passes. It covers the translation-string check, UI and core test typechecks, lint and the dead-code scans. `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` produced no changes to commit.

<details><summary>Review notes</summary>

Pre-reviewed with typescript-expert, testing-expert, frontend-architect and simplicity-engineer agents: 1 round, all approved, no must-fix items. Suggestions taken:
- A narrower type for the image format argument.
- A mapping from rejection reason to message key that the type checker verifies covers every reason.
- A test for the WebP path.
- A clearer CLI hint.

Suggestions not taken, as out of scope or rare:
- Flattening soft-edged images onto a background so they can use JPEG.
- Stepping JPEG down in size.
- Stepping down in size when WebP works but is still over the limit.

The contributor’s second-opinion reviewer was unavailable at submission; the maintainer follow-up above records the subsequent independent review.

</details>
